title: Ultrastrongly coupled open systems and fine grained time
abstract: We study the dynamics of a d-level quantum system coupled to a bosonic reservoir when the coupling constant is large. It is known that in the limit of infinite coupling strength, the system undergoes an instantaneous nonselective measurement, resulting in the immediate decoherence in the measurement basis, followed by a unitary Zeno dynamics. Here we resolve this dynamical process by introducing a fine grained scaling regime of short times proportional to the inverse coupling. We provide a rigorous derivation of the open system dynamics in this regime of ultrastrong coupling and demonstrate how decoherence unfolds continuously in the new time scale. We show that Markovian dynamics which are not given by semigroups arise naturally, in contrast to what happens in the weak coupling theory.
summary: This paper analyzes the time evolution of an open quantum system under ultrastrong coupling by introducing a fine-grained time scale. It resolves the predicted instantaneous decoherence into a continuous process, demonstrating that the resulting dynamics are Markovian but require specialized mathematical tools beyond standard weak-coupling theories.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum dynamics of a system coupled to a reservoir under ultrastrong coupling, aiming to resolve instantaneous decoherence predicted in the infinite coupling limit.
main_result: The evolution is shown to be continuous in a fine-grained time scale ($	au = \lambda t$), and the resulting dynamics are Markovian but not necessarily described by a standard semigroup structure.
method: The authors employ rigorous mathematical derivations using a fine-grained scaling regime, analyzing the system's reduced density matrix evolution via specialized propagators and checking for CP-divisibility criteria.
model_or_system: The model is an open quantum system consisting of a $d$-level system ($S$) coupled to a bosonic reservoir ($R$). The interaction strength ($\lambda$) is taken to be very large (ultrastrong coupling).
key_observables: Reduced density matrix $ho_S(	au)$, decoherence function, and the structure of the time evolution map $\Lambda(	au)$.
important_parameters: Coupling constant ($\lambda$), fine-grained time scale ($	au = \lambda t$), and system/reservoir spectral properties.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on introducing a specific fine-grained scaling regime to handle the strong coupling limit, and certain regularity conditions (Assumption R) are required for limiting procedures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates various coupling regimes ($\lambda$ vs $\Delta$), emphasizing the necessity of the fine-grained time scale $	au$ for resolving instantaneous decoherence in the ultrastrong regime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical problem across different coupling limits, then deriving the dynamics in the fine-grained time limit ($	au = \lambda t$), and finally analyzing the mathematical properties of this evolution map concerning quantum Markovianity (CP-divisibility).
why_interesting: This work tackles a fundamental issue in open quantum systems: how to correctly describe dynamics when coupling strengths are so large that standard weak-coupling approximations fail, providing rigorous tools for non-Markovian/ultrastrong regimes.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Different coupling regimes: From noninteracting to Zeno. Here, λ is the coupling parameter and ∆represents a typical system Bohr frequency, a hopping matrix element in the system Hamiltonian, or similar. The ultraweak and ultrastrong coupling regimes are dynamical regimes involving rescaled times. Here we introduce the fine grained time τ for the ultrastrong coupling regime and we derive the system dynamics as a function of τ. We show that the instantaneous decoherence process known to happen in the Zeno limit (‘λ = ∞’) is resolved as a continuous dynamical process in the fine grained time.
